Subject: VPC license anchoring and burst-cap model

Hi Lauren — great to meet earlier this week. Per our conversation I wanted to outline two pragmatic commercial approaches for SentryHealth's private deployment (VPC + on-prem ingest):

1) Capacity-anchored (node) license + platform fee
   - Commit to reserved node count (e.g., 10 nodes) for predictable throughput and a fixed monthly platform fee.
   - Burst capacity handled via metered overage at a per-token-equivalent rate or pre-bought burst credits.

2) Consumption-forward (metered) with soft-floor platform fee
   - Lower upfront commitment; consumption billed per-token with a small monthly platform retainer to cover control plane/observability.
   - Optional committed spend tier that unlocks support SLAs and volume discounts.

Key trade-offs we discussed: predictability vs. unit economics, and how to handle occasional high-burst windows (quarterly processing jobs). I attached a concise term sheet that shows example pricing bands for both approaches and a sample support-tier mapping (Standard / Premium / Enterprise).

Next steps I suggest: you and your procurement team pick the approach that maps to your risk tolerance; we can then run 2-3 model scenarios against your 12-month forecast to show the true blended effective cost. I can have Ben (SE) map burst sizing for the quarterly jobs after you share the spike profile.

Attachment: Redwood_VPC_Term_Sheet_v2.pdf (term sheet, pricing examples, support tiers)

Best,

Hi Lauren — good questions. Short answers up front, details below:

- Node definition: billing is by "licensed node" which maps to an operational capacity unit (host-level). We can map to your infra by SKU (A10 host = 1 licensed node, 4xA30 host = 1 licensed node with higher throughput credit) — Ben will include the exact equivalency table.
- Burst credits: yes, credits can be purchased up-front and pooled across months and regions under the same enterprise account. They expire on a 12-month horizon unless tied to a committed spend schedule.
- Support: Standard = business-hours support + 24h ticket SLA; Enterprise = 24/7 on-call escalation, 1h P1 response, quarterly architecture reviews, and an assigned technical account manager.

Pricing options (high level) — see attached term sheet for numbers: 
A) 12-month node commit: 10 licensed nodes, $XXk/node/month, platform fee $YYk/month (SLA: Enterprise with annual prepay). Includes 10% monthly burst credit allocation.
B) Metered + soft-floor: platform fee $ZZk/month, per-token pricing with committed spend tiers unlocking 15–25% volume discounts. Burst capacity billed at a predictable per-token rate or via pre-purchased credit packs.

I'll summarize the financial delta in a 12-month blended spreadsheet if you can share your monthly Q1–Q4 consumption estimate. If you prefer, we can run both models and show a break-even month for the commit.

Attachment: Redwood_VPC_Term_Sheet_v2.pdf

Thanks — Ben, can you confirm host->node equivalency and estimated token throughput for the spike Lauren mentioned? Vanessa, want to flag anything on commercial levers we should consider (implementation credit, pilot pricing)?

Best,
Neha

Lauren — quick technical note on the host equivalency and burst behavior so procurement can model cost: 

- Equivalency: we use an effective-TPU-ish throughput metric mapped to common cloud SKUs. Rough mapping: 8xA10 host ~= 1 licensed node baseline; 4xA30 host ~= 1 licensed node but with ~1.8x throughput credit because of higher FP performance. We will provide an exact table once you confirm host image/driver/kernel version.

- Burst mechanics: burst credits are consumed after the committed node pool is saturated for that minute. Credits are drawn from the account-wide pool; they do not change scheduling or priority (they only affect billing). For pipeline jobs that run infrequently (e.g., nightly batches), we typically recommend a small committed node buffer + pre-purchased credit pack sized to the historical 95th percentile of your spikes.

- Ops note: if you require guaranteed low-p99 latency during spikes, we recommend the Enterprise SLA + dedicated on-call, since soft-floor metered plans don't guarantee capacity headroom.

Happy to run the throughput calc if you send a sample trace (token/sec) and job concurrency.

— Ben

1) Pilot/discount ask: SentryHealth requests a 3-month pilot at 30% off the list platform fee for the first 90 days to validate throughput and ROI, with a mutual option to convert the pilot fees into committed node prepay credit if we convert to the 12-month commit.
2) Implementation credit: request a $50k implementation credit applied to first invoice if we sign for 10+ nodes.
3) Invoice cadence: prefer quarterly invoicing rather than monthly for committed nodes.

Attached: SentryHealth_request_redlines_marked.docx — we've highlighted preferred language on platform fee amortization and credit rollover.

If Redwood is agreeable on (1) and (2), we can fast-track an internal approval and return a signed term sheet + PO within 7 business days. Otherwise please let us know the best alternative.
